summary:
**Outpost Commander** is an educational, turn-based strategy game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Challenge CH-03: “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.”

Players command a lunar or Martian outpost and manage its survival for 30 turns. They must balance four interconnected systems: Life Support, Energy Management, Food Production, and Radiation Protection. Every decision has consequences, as improving one system may increase pressure on others.

The game features an isometric 3D-style base, limited actions per turn, and strategic choices such as building solar panels, upgrading batteries, growing crops, recycling water, repairing habitats, and adding radiation shielding.

**Real NASA Data Integration:**
- NASA POWER: Solar irradiance data to influence energy generation.
- NASA DONKI: Solar flare events that create radiation challenges.
- NASA Image and Video Library: Real space images with credits.
- NASA/JPL orbital elements: An interactive orrery on the mission selection screen.

The game uses cached sample data when services are unavailable and clearly labels offline data.

After each mission, players receive a debrief showing system performance and explaining the impact of their decisions.
details:
Outpost Commander is an educational strategy game that transforms space exploration concepts into an interactive survival experience. Players command a lunar or Martian outpost for 30 turns, making decisions that affect crew survival and base stability.

The game features an isometric 3D-style environment and four interconnected systems: Life Support, Energy, Food Production, and Radiation Protection. Players can construct solar panels, upgrade batteries, build greenhouses, recycle water, repair habitats, and install shielding. Each action has resource trade-offs, teaching players systems thinking and strategic resource management.

The project integrates real NASA resources:

  • NASA POWER for solar irradiance data.
  • NASA DONKI for solar flare events.
  • NASA Image and Video Library for authentic space imagery.
  • JPL Horizons for orbital data and the interactive orrery.

When online services are unavailable, cached sample data is clearly identified as offline data.

After each mission, a debrief explains how decisions affected the outpost and visualizes system performance over time.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. Its creative approach combines strategy gaming, real space data, and interactive learning to help students understand the challenges of sustaining human settlements beyond Earth.

The team considered usability, accessibility, resource balance, educational value, and clear data-source attribution. The prototype uses simplified educational calculations rather than claiming scientific simulation accuracy.
